title: A norm separates two geometric objects with no arrow between them
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $A,B$ be commutative $k$-algebras. Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with $k$-morphisms $s,t:R\to U$, $e:U\to R$, $i:R\to R$ and $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ [def-pc-fibre-product] defining a groupoid on $H$-points, naturally in each $k$-scheme $H$, with source $s$, target $t$, identity $e$, inverse $i$ and composition $c$. Assume $s,t$ are finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free], and write $\sigma=s^\sharp,\tau=t^\sharp:A\to B$. For any $k$-algebra map $\alpha_1:A\to k$, set $E_1=B\otimes_{A,\sigma,\alpha_1}k$ [def-weil-module-base-change] and
$$\mathcal B_1=\{\beta:B\to k\text{ a }k\text{-algebra map}:\beta\sigma=\alpha_1\}.$$
The algebra $E_1$ is finite dimensional over $k$, all its prime ideals are maximal with residue field canonically $k$ [def-weil-residue-field], and their corresponding $k$-points identify with $\mathcal B_1$. This set is finite and nonempty (it contains the identity arrow at $\alpha_1$). If $\alpha_0:A\to k$ is another $k$-algebra map and no $\beta\in\mathcal B_1$ satisfies $\beta\tau=\alpha_0$, then there exists $f\in A$ such that
$$\alpha_0(f)=0,\qquad (\beta\tau)(f)\ne0\quad(\beta\in\mathcal B_1).$$
For this same $f$, let $g=N_\sigma(\tau(f))\in A$ denote the norm section whose restrictions to finite-free affine charts are the multiplication determinants [lem-pd-finite-locally-free-norm-charts, def-weil-endomorphism-determinant]. Then
$$\alpha_0(g)=0,\qquad\alpha_1(g)\ne0.$$
The assertion allows nonreduced fibre algebras, varying local ranks, and stabilizers; it makes no assumption that the two points agree on invariant functions.

proof.text: Install the A-actions induced by sigma and alpha_1. Finiteness of s gives a finite A-module B by IsFinite.SpecMap_iff. Mathlib Module.Finite.base_change makes E=k tensor_A B finite dimensional over k. IsArtinianRing.of_finite k E then makes E Artinian, so its spectrum is finite and every prime is maximal. This entirely algebraic argument does not require the affine scheme pullback formula or finite scheme fibres.

proof.text: For every prime P of E, its residue field is a finite E-module because P is maximal, and hence a finite k-module. The structural k-map is bijective by [lem-pc-finite-extension-alg-closed]. Compose its inverse with the residue map to obtain a k-point with kernel P. Two k-points f,g with ker(f) contained in ker(g) agree: apply g to x-algebraMap(k,E)(f(x)). Thus taking the kernel is a bijection from k-points to primes. Tensor universality (AlgHom.liftEquiv) identifies these k-points with beta sigma=alpha_1; sigma being a k-map ensures that restriction to 1 tensor b is a k-map for the original B-structure. This gives the required equivalence, the evaluation equation and uniqueness. Transfer spectrum finiteness along it. The equation e followed by s=id and compatibility of s with k imply that e-sharp is a k-map. Composing it with alpha_1 supplies exactly the stated identity witness.

proof.text: Index the ideals ker(beta tau) by the finite nonempty source-point set, with the identity as a chosen index. If ker(alpha_0) were contained in their union, [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] would put it inside one of them. The scalar-subtraction kernel argument above would then give beta tau=alpha_0, a contradiction. Take f in ker(alpha_0) outside the union. This directly gives both required evaluations of f, including repeated targets and stabilizers.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pd-finite-locally-free-norm-charts] on the top open to the global section corresponding to tau(f). Transport its norm section through GammaSpecIso to g in A and combine the two section restrictions by presheaf functoriality. On a chart containing x, use the existing proved mem_basicOpen_normAt_of_free theorem, which transports [lem-pd-finite-free-norm-prime-criterion] to the scheme fibre. Restricting basic opens and basicOpen_eq_of_affine give g outside x if and only if tau(f) is outside every prime y with s(y)=x.

proof.text: For x_0=ker(alpha_0), the identity beta_0=alpha_0 e-sharp has s(y_0)=x_0 and tau(f) in y_0=ker(beta_0). The norm nonvanishing equivalence therefore forces alpha_0(g)=0. For x_1=ker(alpha_1), take any prime Q of B over x_1. In B/Q one has sigma(a)=alpha_1(a): the difference comes from a-algebraMap(k,A)(alpha_1(a)), which belongs to ker(alpha_1). Thus its A-module structure factors through k. Finiteness over A implies finiteness over k by Module.Finite.of_restrictScalars_finite. Its structural k-map is bijective by [lem-pc-finite-extension-alg-closed], so its inverse composed with B to B/Q gives a k-map beta with kernel Q and beta sigma=alpha_1. The separation property of f makes tau(f) outside Q. Apply the norm equivalence to get alpha_1(g) nonzero. No reducedness, equal invariant values, or common chart rank is used.

The item is the 03BL part (2) argument after base change to k; its conclusion alpha_0(g)=0 is stronger than Stacks' 'g not a unit' and holds because of the identity arrow. Step 1: s is finite by def-pc-finite-locally-free, so B is a finite A-module and E_1 is finite-dimensional; 01I4, 01WL and 02NU give a finite fibre. Step 2: E_1/P is a field (domain node), equal to k (algebraically-closed node); the tensor universal property identifies the points with B_1, and alpha_1 e^# shows B_1 is nonempty. Step 3: prime avoidance (00DS) with r>=1, prime I_j and the explicit h_j witnesses. Step 4 had one gap: it equated the points of R over u_1 with the primes of E_1, but step 1 only identifies Spec E_1 with the fibre-product scheme, and s^{-1}V=Spec F was not justified. FIX: step 4 now uses that s is affine (finite), that E_1 = B/sigma(ker alpha_1)B, and that ker alpha_1 is maximal, so these points are exactly the ker beta with beta in B_1. Only step 4 changes; proof_deps is unchanged. Step 5: the prime of beta_0 = alpha_0 e^# lies over u_0 and contains tau(f); the contrapositive of the norm-prime criterion gives alpha_0(g)=0. Edge cases tested: Spec(k x k) with only identity arrows, k[eps]/eps^2, mu_p in characteristic p, A=0, alpha_0=alpha_1.
